thread:
ashley: Heads up — noticed analytics on the org dashboard showing spikes for another customer after yesterday's canary. looks like telemetry batching is mixing org envelopes when switcher flips quickly.

maria: ugh. repro steps?

ashley: repro: login as admin@org-a, open org switcher, flip to org-b and back rapidly while interacting with insights. metrics panel shows org-b's request counts in org-a's dashboard for ~30s.

tariq: can you paste logs of the telemetry batch id and envelope headers? curious if x-org-id is being lost before batching.

ashley: pasted snippet from browser console:

```
telemetry.batch = [{ event: 'route_hit', headers: { 'x-org-id': 'org-b', 'x-request-id': 'req_9f3' }}]
// next flush: envelope.metadata.orgid: null
```

ashley: server side shows flush without org-id, and batch attributed to the lastSeenOrg in session store.

kevin: we added client-side batching to reduce events. looks like localStorage lastOrg race when switcher updates after the event queue is sampled. we'll need to bind org id to each event immutably at creation.

maria: is this strictly a client bug or also server? if server accepts batches without org header and uses session cookie, we could be double counting.

tariq: server side telemetry pipeline uses a small windowed aggregator that groups envelopes per customer key. if envelope missing org, it falls back to session. that's the surface here.

ashley: UX impact is bad — customers see possible cross-tenant spikes. We need an interim mitigation for the canary: reject batched envelopes missing org header and log metrics to a quarantine queue.

kevin: agree. quick fix: (1) client bind org id immutably into event payload at creation time; (2) proxy middleware to drop batches without org headers and return 400; (3) server tagging so we don't reassign from session fallback.

maria: +1. add a FEATURE_FLAG to gate the strict reject so canary doesn't cause mass 400s. roll it to internal first.

tariq: also need to patch telemetry aggregator to emit a drilldown metric showing "orphaned_envelopes" per minute so SRE can monitor.

kevin: I'll draft the proxy middleware patch. snippet:

```
// proxy middleware
if (!req.headers['x-org-id']) {
  // quarantine
  res.status(400).json({ error: 'missing org header in telemetry batch' });
  log.warn('telemetry: missing org header', { requestId: req.headers['x-request-id'] });
  return;
}
next();
```

ashley: heads-up to support: please explain we observed batching race during canary and we're rolling a safe reject to prevent cross-tenant bleed. will follow up with timeline.

devops-bot: Deploy scheduled: proxy/telemetry-mw v0.4.1 -> canary in us-west at 22:00 UTC. ETA 10m.

maria: tests — we should add e2e that simulates rapid org switch and ensures no events leak. simple puppeteer flow to flip switch and assert per-org counters.

tariq: also add unit test for aggregator fallback logic: if envelope.org is falsy, aggregator must mark as orphan and not attribute to session.

kevin: on it. i'll open PRs: proxy (#4852), client batching guard (#4853), aggregator metric (#4854). tagging @oncall for post-deploy watch.

ashley: thanks — priority P1 for the canary. will paste customer-facing note once we have rollout schedule.

kevin: PRs up, requesting reviews.

maria: quick reminder — update rollout UX doc: mention telemetry atomicity and sticky state hazards when client caches last-org. we should recommend event-level immutability in docs.

ashley: perfect. closing loop once canary green. :thumbsup:
